notes:
disagreement: assigned_to on cases 15 and 33: A IN (54, 67) (both keep their current assignees, expected 2), B = 52 (neither given to Casey Green, expected 0); chose IN (54, 67) because both are right and it is tighter: the request reassigns only the draft and ready cases, so the two closed_incomplete cases are not reassigned to anyone, Casey Green included.
'Shifted to the head office' names no record and is context only: the group Casey Green must join is fixed by the cases' assignment group (HR Service Desk, group 4), because the policy makes an assignee a member of the case's group. Joining Onsite Support HQ (group 6) is neither required nor forbidden.
Seed notifications carry case-status values in their status column (draft, ready, closed_complete and so on), read as the policy's alert 'with case status'; each alert is expected to carry its case's current status. The benchmark check does not test this cell, and seed notifications do not always match their case's status.
Seed notifications go to personal addresses; the alerts here use Casey Green's work address, as the benchmark check does.
The membership's org_id is not tested: the seed's member rows take the group's org, but the request does not fix it.
